Custom runtimes and `sst pulumi dev`; custom domains and a live `sst dev` for `WebFunction`; workflows started from a queue; shared invoke permissions for API Gateway and managed policies for links; and fixes for `sst dev`, Python containers, provider globals and domain redirects. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

Thanks to [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip), who sent seven of the pull requests below, each with an issue that set out the problem first, and to [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya), who sent five, carrying fixes from SST's repository. The authors of the SST pull requests they carry, and the people who reported the problems, are named with each one.

### ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **`sst dev`'s server listens on `127.0.0.1`, at a random port, with a token in its path.** 4.25.0 listened on every interface from port 13557. What the CLI starts gets the address in `SST_SERVER`, as before. A script or tool that called the fixed port, or called it from another machine, has to read `SST_SERVER` instead. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- **The SST Console's local logs connect only from your machine, and only from console.sst.dev.** `sst dev` serves the Console's connection on `localhost:13557`, and on `14557` over TLS, on a listener of its own that takes nothing but the Console's page, and no longer answers on your network. The first time, Chrome asks whether console.sst.dev may connect to your device: allow it to see your local logs. **If you ran `sst cert` before, run it again.** The root certificate it installed kept its private key on your machine; the new one deletes it, and `sst dev` warns until you do. `sst cert --remove` takes the root certificate out, and `SST_NO_CONSOLE=1` turns the local server off. ([75fc620](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/commit/75fc62006))
- **Provider settings that are booleans or numbers now reach the provider.** 4.25.0 dropped settings like `aws: { maxRetries: 5 }` or `skipCredentialsValidation: true` without a word. Now they're applied, so the first deploy after you upgrade may show the default provider updated. Check `providers` in your `app()` for such settings before you deploy. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- **A deploy refuses a stage whose state is missing,** when the home's history says it was deployed, where 4.25.0 created every resource again. Set `SST_ALLOW_MISSING_STATE=true` to go on anyway. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- **A function whose handler file isn't there fails the deploy,** in `sst dev`, and in `sst deploy` for a function with its own `bundle`. 4.25.0 deployed it, and the function failed when it was invoked. Fix the handler path the error names. ([#262](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/262), by [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya), carrying [anomalyco/sst#6681](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6681) by [@anatolzak](https://github.com/anatolzak), who reported it in [anomalyco/sst#6680](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6680))

### New

- **Custom runtimes:** a function can take a runtime made of commands, for a language SST doesn't build, with `sst.runtime({ lambda, build, dev, watch })`. Its build command builds the function, and its dev command runs it in `sst dev`. The docs have a [Custom Runtimes](https://sst-community.github.io/sst/docs/custom-runtimes/) page, with Go and .NET. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- **`sst pulumi dev`** brings SST's dev loop to a plain Pulumi project: it deploys a dev stack with your own `pulumi up`, runs the functions `sst.dev.yaml` names on your machine from their source, and runs its dev commands beside it. A plain `pulumi up` puts the deployed code back. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- **A component written with Pulumi's own `ComponentResource`** can report to `sst dev` with an `_sst` output: a command for a pane, and a URL to show after a deploy. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- **`sst.aws.WebFunction` serves a custom domain** through CloudFront with `domain`. The endpoint then uses IAM authorization, with CloudFront signing its requests, so clients of the domain sign nothing; `url` is the domain's URL, and the endpoint is `endpointUrl`. A deploy role with limited permissions needs to manage CloudFront, ACM in `us-east-1`, and DNS records. ([#276](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/276), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#274](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/274))
- **`sst.aws.WebFunction` can test the real endpoint in `sst dev`,** with `dev: { live: true }`. `sst dev` deploys the real function and endpoint with a bridge that sends each request to your local server and streams the response back, so IAM authorization, callers in AWS and webhooks work against it. Without it, `sst dev` is unchanged. ([#275](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/275), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#273](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/273))
- **A workflow can be started from an SQS queue.** Subscribe a workflow to a queue for short executions, or use `workflow.dispatcher()` for longer ones, with fair queues per tenant through `MessageGroupId`. ([#243](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/243), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip))
- **`ApiGatewayV2`, `ApiGatewayV1` and `ApiGatewayWebSocket` have `addHandler`,** so routes share one Lambda invoke permission instead of each adding a statement to the function's resource policy, which fails the deploy once an API has enough routes on one function. ([#217](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/217), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#215](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/215))
- **`sst.aws.Function` takes `linkPermissions`,** to move its linked resources' grants into customer-managed IAM policies, for a function that links enough resources to go over IAM's 10,240-character limit on a role's inline policies. Using it needs a deploy role that can manage IAM policies, and switching an existing function takes two deploys, with `retainInline: true`. ([#218](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/218), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#216](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/216))
- **`sst dev` writes one log per function,** in `.sst/log/lambda/`, rotated by size, in place of a file per invocation. Each line has its time and request ID, so `tail -f` follows a function and `grep -r` follows a request. `SST_DEV_INVOCATION_LOGS` and `SST_DEV_INVOCATION_LOGS_TOTAL` set the limits, or turn the files off. The per-invocation files of earlier sessions are removed when `sst dev` next starts. ([#283](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/283), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#279](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/279))
- **The CLI looks for a newer release once a day,** in the background, within its major version, and says so after a run. Not in CI, and `SST_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK` turns it off. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))

### Fixes

- **`sst dev` no longer holds a file open for every file in the project on macOS.** It watches with FSEvents. A project whose path has `node_modules` anywhere in it, like `~/code/node_modules-demo/app`, is watched now, and so are folders in `watch.paths` that are hidden or named `node_modules`. ([#280](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/280), by [@rogueturnip](https://github.com/rogueturnip); [#278](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/278), [#281](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/281))
- **Python container builds work when a uv workspace member is above the workspace root,** like `../../lib`. A layout that would collide or leave the build context fails with an error that names the members. ([#271](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/271), by [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya), carrying [anomalyco/sst#6929](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6929) by [@chrislambert](https://github.com/chrislambert), who reported it in [anomalyco/sst#6928](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6928))
- **A dependency that declares a top-level name matching a provider no longer breaks the deploy** with `The symbol "random" has already been declared`. ([#269](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/269), by [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya); [anomalyco/sst#6979](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6979), reported by [@chinigo](https://github.com/chinigo))
- **`sst dev` no longer crashes on a `Service` container without a `dev.command`,** and says what's wrong with an empty or badly quoted command in its pane. A `dev.command` on a `Service` with `containers` runs when no container has its own. ([#267](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/267), by [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya), carrying [anomalyco/sst#6945](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6945) by [@mkilp](https://github.com/mkilp), who reported it in [anomalyco/sst#6944](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6944))
- **A domain's redirects keep the path and the query string.** The redirect is answered by the distribution's CloudFront function, so repeated and encoded parameters survive, and the redirect distribution has no HTTP-only origin. ([#265](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/265), by [@AlperSakarya](https://github.com/AlperSakarya), carrying [anomalyco/sst#7047](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7047) by [@mikkopori](https://github.com/mikkopori); [anomalyco/sst#7022](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/7022), reported by [@herre-ixxi](https://github.com/herre-ixxi))
- **`sst dev --mode=basic` no longer exits as it starts,** when its UI asked for events before the server was ready. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))

### Also

- `sst dev` stages get a new stub object once, on their first `sst dev` with this release, as with any release whose bridge code changes. Deployed stages are untouched. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- A run that crashes now leaves its lock in two places. This version's `sst unlock` clears both, and 4.25.0's clears one, so on a team where some still run 4.25.0, a stage that one of them unlocked may need `sst unlock` once more with this version. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))
- A component's error reads as it's written, without Pulumi's "while serializing property" in front. ([#272](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/272))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.26.0
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.26.0"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
